family.tagline: One Companion Core in the library lounge, and four people who use it.
family.story: Claire is a hospital administrator, and Etienne writes game-engine code from the garden room. Hugo, seventeen, plays upstairs, and Lea, twelve, reads and studies in her room. All four share one Companion Core.

companion.name: Tansy
companion.job: Drafts Claire’s replies to the school office and the dentist from her notes.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Claire reads each one and sends it herself.

companion.name: Sparrow
companion.job: Drafts Etienne’s messages to his playtesters from his rough notes.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Etienne reads each message and sends it himself.

popup.title: Etienne carries the parcel in
popup.body: A parcel waits on the tiled porch. Etienne carries the Companion Core to the Library Lounge, where Claire clears a shelf.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Lea reads the guide aloud while Hugo lifts the Core out.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Hugo plugs in the cable and Lea presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: Etienne opens the Wi-Fi settings on his phone, joins the Core’s own network, and then chooses the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agent and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Claire picks Hermes, and the family adds Paperless-ngx and Forgejo. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Claire’s agent answers to Tansy
popup.body: Claire messages the agent she named Tansy. The reply comes back from the Core on its shelf.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: claire
say.text: Good morning, Claire. This is Tansy. Where shall we start?

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: The morning post gets scanned
popup.body: Claire scans the morning post. Paperless-ngx reads and tags every page on the Core, not in a rented drive, so one word finds the invoice.

beats.capability: read ebooks in your browser, with notes and highlights; your library lives on your Core

popup.title: Lea and Claire share a novel
popup.body: After school, Lea and Claire share the chesterfield and one novel. Koodo Reader opens the family’s ebooks in a browser, and the highlights Lea makes stay on the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: The dentist gets an answer
popup.body: The dentist asks Claire to confirm a time. She tells Tansy yes, and Tansy writes the reply on the Core’s local model. Claire reads it, then sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose. Companion Agents are in beta.

say.speaker: claire
say.text: Here is the draft for the dentist. Please read it first.

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: The plan bends around a meeting
popup.body: When the staff rota meeting moves to Monday, Claire gives the review a new block in Companion Planning. The plan is one local file on the Core.

beats.capability: track accounts, budgets, bills and savings goals, with rules that sort your transactions

popup.title: Claire teaches the ledger a rule
popup.body: On Sunday morning at the kitchen island, Claire writes one rule in Firefly III. Lunch transactions now sort into the lunches budget, in a ledger Claire keeps on the Core.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains at the DNS level for devices on your network

popup.title: Etienne explains the quieter recipe page
popup.body: Lea asks why her tablet’s cake recipe shows fewer ads. Etienne says the tablet asks Pi-hole on the Core first, and domains on its block lists get no answer.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book and meal planner for the household

popup.title: The pesto jar joins the list
popup.body: The pesto jar is empty again. Hugo adds it to the family’s KitchenOwl list, and Claire sees the new line before she leaves for the shops.

beats.capability: host your own git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: The chaise is Etienne’s desk
popup.body: On the chaise, Etienne opens an issue for the stuck door a playtester found. Forgejo keeps the issue and the fix on the Core, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Sparrow’s draft needs one change
popup.body: At the potting bench, Etienne leaves Sparrow two lines for playtesters. Sparrow drafts it on the Core’s local model, and Etienne reads it, fixes a line, then sends it himself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: etienne
say.text: The playtest note is ready. Please read it, then send it.

beats.capability: write and run notebooks, code and data in a browser, on your Core

popup.title: Etienne finds three seeds for Hugo
popup.body: Etienne tries a cave generator in a JupyterLab notebook, and three seeds come out worth showing Hugo. The notebook runs its code on the Core.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals

popup.title: Watering joins the household board
popup.body: In the front garden, Etienne adds the planters to the household board in Yuvomi. Hugo ticks off the watering after school, and Claire sees it done.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: The games live on the Core
popup.body: Saturday morning on his bed, Hugo opens his Steam library in a browser. Steam Headless runs the session on the Core, and the games install there.
popup.note: Steam needs a Valve account. A Core may lack the graphics power a game wants.

beats.capability: model low-poly 3D art in your browser

popup.title: Hugo models the game’s lantern
popup.body: Cross-legged on the platform bed, Hugo shapes a low-poly lantern in Blockbench for his father’s game. The Core serves the editor, which opens in his browser.

beats.capability: host your own git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: The lantern goes to his father
popup.body: Hugo exports the lantern and opens a pull request in Forgejo. Etienne reviews it from the Garden Room, then merges it before lunch.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: Lea writes the last line herself
popup.body: Stuck on a poem’s last line, Lea tries three endings in Obsidian and keeps the one that rhymes. Her notes are plain Markdown files on the Core.

beats.capability: read Wikipedia and other reference sites offline

popup.title: The balloon question gets answered
popup.body: Lea looks up how a hot-air balloon rises in Kiwix. The Wikipedia file was downloaded once, so the Core answers and no search engine sees the question.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: Lea checks her dinner menu
popup.body: On her bed, Lea writes Saturday’s dinner menu in Italian for the family, then checks it in LibreTranslate. Its language models were downloaded once, and the Core does the work.

popup.title: Four people share one Core
popup.body: Letters, code, games and schoolwork share one Companion Core in the Library Lounge.

closing.body: Your paperwork, code and homework questions can sit on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: The Library Lounge and the Garden Room both answer living and office. Every beat that names a room sets nth: the Library Lounge is first (larger), the Garden Room second.
The Library Lounge has no desk or TV. Claire anchors on the Core, the chesterfield and the room; the media beat is Koodo Reader at the chesterfield. No beat says TV, screen or desk there.
The Garden Room has a chaise, a potting bench and an armchair, no desk. Etienne anchors on the chaise (couch, second instance) and the room; the text names only the chaise and the potting bench.
Hugo’s room has a platform bed and no screen. Beats say laptop and browser, never a screen. Steam carries the Valve-account and graphics-power note.
Blockbench is told as the Core serving a browser editor; no beat says where its files are saved. Hugo’s export then goes to Forgejo, so its home is the repository.

Neither companion has Companion Memory connected, so no beat names it. Both agents are Hermes; each beat names who reads and who sends. The Companion Agents beta line sits on Claire’s second Hermes beat.
Pi-hole is told as one household resolver the router points at, covering only devices that use it for DNS. No parental-control wording.
